Findings. All 36 sourceIssues now carry verdicts and all 36 are confirmed: 29 misprints, 5 errors and 2 gaps. I located every quoted string in the source and checked every argument. Not one failed.

The five errors and two gaps. E1: the degree of a filtered (phi,N,G_K)-module is printed as t_N - t_H twice on p. 32, and three independent checks force t_H - t_N - the paper's own semistability convention on p. 14 (mu(E') <= mu(E) for strict subobjects) together with Definition 5.1's 'weakly admissible = semistable of slope 0' and Fontaine's t_H(M') <= t_N(M'); Remark 5.5(ii), which makes acyclicity equivalent to H^1 of the associated bundle vanishing; and the rank-one example M = F with phi(e) = pe and one jump at 0, where X_st(M) = B_cris^{phi=p^{-1}} = 0 and X_dR is nonzero, so the module is not acyclic although the printed formula gives degree +1. I redid that computation independently of the extraction. E3: Corollary 3.21(iv) is refuted by the paper's own footnote 9 on the same page, which exhibits U_1/Q_p t_x with ht 0 and curvature > 0; it is a quotient of itself, so (iv) would force curvature 0, and section 3.2.7's computation Hom_BC(U_1/Q_p t_x, V_1) = 0 rules that out. E4: the fourth bullet of section 3.2.2 bounds the slopes of an extension from one-sided hypotheses on the two terms, which fails at once for O(5) and O on the Fargues-Fontaine curve; the printed sentence also opens with an untranslated French 'Il'. E5: Lemma 4.24(i) asserts Ext^1_TVS(U_d,W) = W while its own proof concludes h^1(U_d) = 0 with h^1 = Ext^1_TVS, and part (ii) needs the vanishing. E31: Corollary 3.20(b) omits the nonvanishing hypothesis, the zero object having curvature < 0 and height 0. The two gaps are E32, where the reduction of Lemma 3.16 to lambda > 0 does not exclude a U_0 = Q_p summand, since Q_p is a subobject of V_1 and not a quotient, and E36, where Lemma 4.29 claims C-linearity for all c in O_C while the proof takes c in O_C^*.

Two of the misprints deserve recording for the method that settled them, because they are the kind a reader can only confirm by counting. E8 flags an Ext^{1,natural} whose superscript is defined nowhere: I counted the natural sign in the whole 61-page text and it occurs exactly once, at that spot. E13 and E15 are the same shape: 'spherically closed' occurs once against four occurrences of 'spherically complete', and 'Topological Pair' occurs once against thirteen of 'Topological Vector Space'. The remaining twenty-six misprints are each contradicted by the paper's own neighbouring text, and I checked each in place: the reversed inequality at the end of Lemma 3.16's proof against the goal stated three lines earlier; B_st for B^+_st in Proposition 5.20, where the printed map is not defined; a filtration 'containing' where Lemma 5.3 supplies one contained; M_K for M^*_K in Example 5.11; a stray tower index in (8.7), whose fully indexed companion is (8.8); a reference to (6.11) where only (8.8) can be inverse-limited; perfectness attributed to the outer complex rather than the coefficients in Lemma 8.13; b_{i,k-1} for b_{i,k-i}; H^r_et for H^r_proet in Corollary 6.19, which is about Stein and affinoid varieties; J_j for J_i and h_i for h_j in section 7; f_i for f_r and H^i_dR for H^r_dR in the proof of Theorem 6.4; the lattice argument of Remark 6.13(i); the unsatisfiable range '0 <= j <= j - 1' in Lemma 2.10; V for V_1 in Lemma 5.12; B_m for B_1 in section 3.2.7; mismatched indices in Remark 4.20; 'is' for 'if' with the wrong index in Lemma 5.4; a summation index in Proposition 4.27; the leftmost entry of the diagram in Proposition 5.23, fixed by the sentence that follows it; a bound tau against a free sigma in Proposition 4.10; a rebound j in Corollary 2.9; Hom_F(M,F) where the F^nr-dual is meant; and an undefined Y in the proof of Proposition 8.4.
